The coverage map below links every brief requirement and your decisions to planned work. Ticket labels are provisional; **nothing in the plan has changed**.

| Source | Requirement | Planned coverage | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brief: Background | 40 plots; March–October seasons | P02 Garden registry | Exactly 40 stable plot records; explicit season dates |
| Brief: Must 1 | Apply for the coming season with up to three preferred plots | P05 Applications | Application persists; 0–3 distinct preferences accepted; duplicates and invalid plots rejected |
| Brief: Must 2 | Coordinator allocates from applications | P06 Initial allocation | Coordinator reviews preferences and assigns available plots |
| Brief: Must 2 | Move unallocated applicants to a waiting list in application order | P07 Waiting list | Ordering uses original application time, even when applicants enter the list later |
| Brief: Must 3 | Gardener sees their allocated plot and season dates | P08 Allocation views | Correct allocated, waiting, and unallocated states; no access to another household’s data |
| Brief: Must 4 | Gardener reports a problem with their plot | P09 Problem reporting | Own-plot report persists; cross-household submissions rejected |
| Brief: Must 4 | Coordinator sees open problems and resolves them | P09 Problem reporting | Open queue updates after resolution; repeated resolution is safe |
| Brief: Must 5 | Coordinator sees a grid of all 40 plots and their holders | P08 Allocation views | Grid reflects assignments and vacancies; accessible list alternative |
| Brief: Rules | At most one plot per household per season | P02 Registry, P06 Allocation | Database constraints and concurrent allocation tests |
| Brief: Rules | Returning gardeners applying before 1 February receive priority | P05 Applications, P06 Allocation | Previous-season eligibility and cutoff-boundary tests; waiting-list placement cannot bypass priority |
| Brief: Rules | Waiting list is strictly first come, first served | P07 Waiting list | Original application order, deterministic ties, and head-only vacancy allocation |
| Brief: Constraints | Works on phones | P04 Prototype, P05/P08/P09 interfaces, P12 Verification | Owner prototype review and complete phone journey checks |
| Brief: Constraints | Contact details visible only to coordinator | P03 Access, P08 Views, P12 Verification | Server-side permission tests; gardener responses exclude contact details |
| Brief: Constraints | Large text and plain language for less confident users | P04 Prototype, interface tickets, P12 Verification | Readability, keyboard, focus, contrast, and error-recovery checks |
| Your decision | Emailed one-time sign-in links; no passwords | P03 Passwordless access | Expiring, single-use links; replay rejection; resend and failure recovery |
| Your decision | One daily coordinator email listing new problem reports | P10 Daily digest | Scheduled batches; boundary, downtime, retry, and delivery-failure tests |
| Brief: Later | Online plot-fee payment | **Deferred** | No payment integration in the first version |
| Brief: Later | Shared tool-lending shelf | **Deferred** | No lending functionality in the first version |

Supporting work makes those outcomes verifiable: **P01** establishes and enables the verification pipeline; **P11** demonstrates allocation to you; **P12** checks complete journeys and operational recovery; **P13** records your first-version acceptance.

The interpretation separating initial returning-gardener priority from subsequent chronological waiting-list allocation remains a **labelled assumption**, along with the household identity and digest details in the package. Checkpoint tickets remain advisory rather than automatically enforced gates.

Review not rerun: showing the coverage map changes no ticket's scope, dependencies or responsibilities.
